verdict: OK to lend in Moradabad steel & metal utensils — back the e-commerce/export-linked units with tight monthly stock-and-receivable control; avoid the thin-margin, single-buyer job-work units.
title: Moradabad steel & metal utensils: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Moradabad units buy steel and brass strip, stamp and polish it into utensils and ware, and sell into wholesale, export and now e-commerce channels.** Cash is tied in metal inventory and in the receivable cycle; the value sits in finishing quality and buyer relationships, not in the metal itself. The local export base is large — Moradabad's export book is reported at 11,460 crore, with a push to link the brass trade to e-commerce and global markets [1]. **So when a proposal lands, check the buyer mix and the channel split first; if a single buyer or single channel dominates, ask for the last twelve months of invoices by buyer.**

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Working capital is the whole game here.** A rated peer in utensil manufacturing carried working capital intensity of about 53% in FY2025, down from about 66% in FY2024, still elevated on an elongated debtor cycle and African customer risk [8]. **So when a proposal lands, check the debtor days and the export customer geography; if receivables stretch beyond the stated terms, ask for the ageing and the top-five debtor list.** Locally, a steel factory fire in June 2026 [3] and press reporting that UP manufacturing including brass is declining on state neglect [2] tell you asset protection and promoter commitment need a hard look. **Ask for the fire-safety certificate and insurance cover on plant and stock before sanction.**

## The growth opportunity
**The data call is OK (score 88), and UP is the faster half of it.** UP GST collections rose 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide IIP for NIC 25 output is up 16.9% YoY [D]. **Pursue the units that are adding an e-commerce or export channel on top of an existing wholesale book — that is where the local push is going [1].** Peer results support volume-led growth: Kirloskar Ferrous posted revenue up 17% y-o-y in Q2 FY27 [6], Shyam Metalics revenue up 23% with volumes up 24% [7], and Sacheta Metals revenue up 22.06% in FY-2025 [5]. **Avoid the pure job-work units with no own buyer relationship and no channel beyond one trader.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the metal and the receivable, not the balance sheet.** Take a stock-and-book-debt statement every month, with a physical stock check at least quarterly. **Covenant the working capital cycle: if debtor days cross the sanctioned limit for two consecutive months, freeze further drawing power.** Peer margin pressure is real — Kirloskar's EBITDA margin fell on coking coal and rupee depreciation [6], and Ratnamani's Q4 sales fell to INR893 crore from INR1,575 crore on muted demand and Middle East issues [4]. **So price the limit to a 6% operating margin floor, the level at which a rated rolling-mill peer's rating would come under pressure [9].**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the receivable and the stock, monthly.** A rising debtor list with new distant buyers, stock that does not reconcile to the book, or promoter withdrawals are the first signals. **Local sources say little about Moradabad unit-level finances; lean on first principles and these peers.**
watch: Stock shortfall vs book >10% -> freeze drawing power and inspect godown
Debtor ageing and top-five buyer list (monthly)
Debtor days beyond sanctioned limit for 2 months -> stop fresh disbursement
GST turnover below bank sales by >15% -> ask for reconciliation before renewal
Lapsed cover or no certificate -> withhold renewal until produced
Large unexplained withdrawals -> re-appraise and cap limit
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Local reports flag UP brass/manufacturing decline and a steel factory fire; peer margins under input-cost pressure.
